title: The DC-IAM makes debt ceiling increases permissionless but rate-limited, so exposure can only grow at a governance-sanctioned speed
content:
A.3.7.1.1.2.4 states that the Debt Ceiling Instant Access Module "allows **any user** to adjust the Debt Ceiling of a supported vault type according to the rules defined in the DC-IAM smart contract logic and parameters set by the Core Facilitator." Governance sets three bounds per vault type: `line` (maximum ceiling), `gap` (target available debt), and `ttl` (ceiling increase cooldown).

The division of labour is the design. Governance decides the *envelope*; anyone may move the ceiling inside it, so no vote is needed to accommodate ordinary demand. A.3.7.1.1.2.4.1 notes that under this arrangement `line` "essentially replaces the Debt Ceiling parameter" — governance stops setting the operative value and sets only its ceiling-of-the-ceiling.

What makes it safe is that `gap` and `ttl` together bound a *rate*, not a level: A.3.7.1.1.2.4.3 states the two "in combination enforce a maximum rate at which debt usage can increase over time using a given vault type." A.3.7.1.1.2.2 gives the purpose plainly — the methodology "limits the rate at which exposure can increase in a short period of time in the event of an unexpected emergency." An attacker cannot draw the entire `line` at once, however large it is.

A.3.7.1.1.2.4.2 states the trade-off without hedging: "The higher this value, the more risk there is from large collateral drops in very short amounts of time. The smaller this value, the more vault use is negatively affected." `gap` is a direct dial between safety and usability, and the Atlas asks that it accommodate "all reasonable usage" — no more.
description: Any user may raise a vault type's ceiling within the line cap, but gap sets the target headroom and ttl the cooldown, together fixing a maximum rate of debt growth per vault type.
